worked_solution:
First, we compute ${E}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}^{2} & =E\cdot E \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${E}^{2}=E,$ so $E$ is an idempotent matrix. 

We can use this fact to compute ${E}^{4}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}^{4} & ={E}^{2}\cdot {E}^{2} \\  & =E\cdot E \\  & ={E}^{2} \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{E}^{4}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
